items.prompt: Introduce yourself for an entry-level technical role.
rubric: State your current background, one relevant skill and what you want to learn.
items.example: I am a graduate who built a small Python study tool. I tested its core functions and want to improve my database skills.

items.prompt: Describe a situation where you had to learn something unfamiliar.
rubric: Give a specific situation, your action, the result and what you would change.
items.example: I did not know how to test an API, so I wrote a small failing example, read the local documentation and added a regression test.

items.prompt: Describe a challenge using Situation, Task, Action and Result.
rubric: Separate your personal contribution from the team result.
items.example: Our demo failed on empty input. I reproduced it, added validation and tested the fix before the next demo.

items.prompt: Explain one project you personally worked on.
rubric: Explain the user problem, the data flow, your contribution and a limitation.
items.example: My tool stores study notes locally. The interface calls a small API, which writes SQLite rows. I implemented validation; shared-device access remains a limitation.

items.prompt: Explain a small application design and its failure modes.
rubric: State assumptions, components, storage, failure handling and one tradeoff.
items.example: For a small local tracker I would start with one process and SQLite. A backup protects against file loss; concurrent remote use would require revisiting that design.

items.prompt: Explain a retrieval-augmented generation project design.
rubric: Describe ingestion, retrieval, citations, evaluation and a failure case.
items.example: I would chunk permitted documents, retrieve relevant passages and test whether citations support each answer. Missing relevant passages would be reported rather than hidden.

items.prompt: Describe a technical decision and an alternative.
rubric: Name a constraint, compare alternatives, explain the choice and when to revisit it.
items.example: I chose a local database to simplify setup. It limits multi-user concurrency, so I would revisit the choice if remote collaboration became a requirement.
